Birmingham: The Midlands Motorcycle Hub

Birmingham's central location makes it an excellent base for motorcycle weekends in every direction. The Shropshire Hills, Welsh Marches, Peak District, Cotswolds, and Malvern Hills are all within easy reach. The challenge isn't finding good riding — it's choosing which direction to head.

1. Shropshire Hills and Long Mynd (100 miles)

Head west on the A458 through Bridgnorth to Church Stretton. The Long Mynd is an ancient moorland ridge with a stunning road across its summit. The descent to Asterton features steep hairpins with views across the Welsh borders. Continue through the Clun Valley for some of England's quietest lanes. Ludlow, with its castle and Michelin-starred restaurants, makes an excellent overnight.

2. North Wales via the Marches (180 miles)

Follow the A5 west through Shrewsbury to Llangollen. From Llangollen, the Horseshoe Pass is a quick appetiser before heading into Snowdonia on the A5. The Ogwen Valley section is magnificent. Continue to Betws-y-Coed and return via the A470 and A44 through mid-Wales. A full weekend that covers outstanding ground.

3. Cotswolds and Vale of Evesham (110 miles)

Head south on the A46 through Evesham to Broadway. The northern Cotswolds are barely an hour from Birmingham and offer gentle, civilised touring through honey-stone villages. Chipping Campden, Stow-on-the-Wold, and Bourton-on-the-Water are all within a compact area. The B4632 escarpment road offers the best views.

Birmingham riders should look west to Wales and Shropshire — these are some of England and Wales' most underrated motorcycle roads, and they're on your doorstep.

4. Peak District (130 miles)

Head north on the A38 and A515 to Buxton, then explore the Peak District's best roads. The A537 Cat and Fiddle, Snake Pass, and the White Peak lanes around Bakewell and Matlock are all within reach. The route via the Manifold Valley through Hartington adds Staffordshire flavour.

5. Malvern Hills and Wye Valley (120 miles)

Head south-west to the Malvern Hills, then continue to the Wye Valley on the Welsh border. The road along the Wye between Monmouth and Hay-on-Wye follows one of Britain's most beautiful rivers through ancient woodland. The Malvern Hills themselves offer a ridge road with panoramic views east across the Severn Vale and west to Wales.

Practical Tips

  • Shropshire: Overlooked and underrated. Some of the best riding within 60 minutes of Birmingham
  • Cotswolds: Avoid summer weekends. Spring and autumn midweek visits are far more enjoyable
  • Peak District: Accessible but busy. The White Peak lanes are quieter than the Dark Peak main roads
  • Wales: Friday evening departure to Llangollen sets up a perfect weekend
keyTakeaways: Birmingham's central location opens up Shropshire, Wales, the Peak District, the Cotswolds and the Malverns in every direction.
The Shropshire Hills and Long Mynd (100 miles) offer steep hairpins near Asterton and some of England's quietest lanes.
The North Wales via the Marches run (180 miles) links the Horseshoe Pass, the A5 Ogwen Valley and mid-Wales.
The northern Cotswolds are barely an hour away for gentle village touring (110 miles).
Shropshire and the Welsh borders are the standout underrated roads on your doorstep.

faq.q: What is the best underrated ride from Birmingham?
faq.a: The Shropshire Hills and Long Mynd, at 100 miles. Head west on the A458 through Bridgnorth to Church Stretton, then ride the road over the Long Mynd summit with its steep hairpins descending to Asterton. Continue through the quiet Clun Valley and finish in Ludlow, whose castle and fine restaurants make it an excellent overnight. It is superb riding within an hour of the city.

faq.q: How do I reach Snowdonia for a weekend?
faq.a: Take the North Wales via the Marches route (180 miles). Follow the A5 west through Shrewsbury to Llangollen, warm up on the Horseshoe Pass, then head into Snowdonia on the A5 through the magnificent Ogwen Valley to Betws-y-Coed. Return via the A470 and A44 through mid-Wales. A Friday-evening run to Llangollen sets up a perfect weekend.

The Cotswolds and Vale of Evesham loop at 110 miles. Head south on the A46 through Evesham to Broadway; the northern Cotswolds are barely an hour from Birmingham. Chipping Campden, Stow-on-the-Wold and Bourton-on-the-Water sit in a compact area, and the B4632 escarpment road offers the best views. Avoid summer weekends and ride midweek instead.

faq.q: Where can I find river scenery?
faq.a: The Malvern Hills and Wye Valley route (120 miles). Head south-west to the Malverns, whose ridge road gives panoramic views east across the Severn Vale and west to Wales, then continue to the Wye Valley. The road along the Wye between Monmouth and Hay-on-Wye follows one of Britain's most beautiful rivers through ancient woodland.

faq.q: Is the Peak District easy to reach?
faq.a: Yes. Head north on the A38 and A515 to Buxton, around 130 miles for the round trip. From there the A537 Cat and Fiddle, Snake Pass and the White Peak lanes around Bakewell and Matlock are all within reach. The White Peak lanes are noticeably quieter than the busier Dark Peak main roads, and the Manifold Valley through Hartington adds Staffordshire flavour.
